inspections.raw: Failed - First  149 EROSION (56013)  Result by: Technical Services on 01/23/2026 at 12:49 PM
inspections.comments: Technical Services (1/26/2026 8:04 AM) Erosion control measures are required to be in place as soon as any ground disturbance begins and maintained throughout the construction process. Erosion control measures such as a vegetative buffer, silt fence,SOD, or any appropriate Best Management Practice (BMP), as described in the Florida Stormwater Erosion and Sedimentation Control Manual, may be used. The manual can be downloaded at https://www.fsesci.com/downloads/ A vegetative buffer is the most efficient and cost-effective form of erosion control. For most sites, a minimum of 15 ft of undisturbed vegetation is a sufficient buffer. Steep sites may require a larger buffer area. A vegetative buffer can be re-established on a disturbed site with the installation of sod. Silt fence is the commonly used form of erosion control protection. Silt fence needs to be placed so that it includes all areas of fill or disturbed soil, and the silt fence needs to be keyed into the ground (buried/trenched up to the line, you should be able to pull up on the silt fence at any point, and it does not move off the ground). The area from the permitted lot line to the road edge along the ROW along the front has been disturbed, needs erosion protection. There is a large, disturbed area in the adjacent ROW to the right, that needs the disturbed areas restored and stabilized.
